source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Predict attraction or repulsion from static electric charges.

mx.name: term_substitution
mx.teacher_note: static charge is the same as its neighbouring term in this chapter, so the decision does not change.

mx.name: condition_omission
mx.teacher_note: The decision still holds even if we ignore this condition: Use this for objects that have acquired static charge by rubbing or for a charged body brought near another body.

mx.name: relationship_reversal
mx.teacher_note: Two similarly charged balloons attract; opposite charges repel.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: This rule applies even when Use this for objects that have acquired static charge by rubbing or for a charged body brought near another body is not true.

intelligence.enrichment: When certain materials are rubbed together, static charges build up on their surfaces. A charged body can exert electrostatic force on another charged body or on an uncharged body; like charges repel and unlike charges attract. rubbing certain materials -> static charge buildup -> electrostatic attraction or repulsion without contact The learner correctly applies this rule: When certain materials are rubbed together, static charges build up on their surfaces. A charged body can exert electrostatic force on another charged body or on an uncharged body; like charges repel and unlike charges attract. Rubbing makes charged objects sticky, so all charged objects attract every nearby object in the same way.
